strengths: The virtual-correspondence construction offers an original, simple approach to a difficult multiview geometry problem. Reusing established 5-point/6-point and P3P solvers makes the core method accessible and potentially useful in robust estimation. The manuscript appropriately acknowledges that its hypotheses are approximate. :codex-file-citation{path="/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b03/review-experiment-a1lo50eo/call-a168baf1170b45989ea89130dcd9f519/manuscript.pdf" purpose="source"}

The calibrated results demonstrate a meaningful speed–accuracy tradeoff. On PhotoTourism, Table 2 reports AUC@10 of 70.47 at 75.78 ms for M±δ+R+F, versus 70.54 at 105.50 ms for 5pt+P3P. The faster M+R+F variant also improves over the HC baseline in both accuracy and runtime. These results provide the main case for acceptance.

Evaluation is substantial: 5,000 triplets per scene, two real datasets, two RANSAC frameworks, fixed-iteration timing curves, noise and outlier experiments, and component ablations. The supplementary metric covering all three camera pairs addresses relative translation-scale recovery. Separating the parameter-validation scene from the main evaluation strengthens the evidence.
weaknesses: The unknown-focal-length extension has a weaker practical case. In Table 3, 4p3vf(M) achieves AUC@10 of 49.88 at 12.67 ms, versus 56.79 at 11.72 ms for 6pt+P3P. Even the strongest learned variant reaches only 53.56 while taking 259.63 ms. Focal-length estimation errors and direct comparisons with existing 4p3vf solvers on the same data are absent. The results establish feasibility more convincingly than practical advantage.

The geometric bound controls virtual-point epipolar error through triangle size; it does not guarantee a small error or an accurate pose. Figure 10 shows substantial errors even without measurement noise, and Figure 14 confirms scene dependence. The effects of depth variation, viewpoint changes, and triangle conditioning are not isolated, leaving the method’s reliability outside the evaluated settings insufficiently characterized.

The learned component provides little demonstrated benefit after refinement: Table 2 gives essentially identical PhotoTourism accuracy for L+R and M+R, while runtime increases from 74.94 to 297.88 ms. Moreover, Equation (2), presented as the training loss, is signed and lacks a square or absolute value; minimizing it literally would not encourage zero epipolar error. This is a localized formulation and reproducibility concern for the learned branch.

Some evaluation details remain insufficiently specified, including numerical inlier thresholds and the oracle-specific RANSAC stopping modification. Section 9.7 and Table 7 reverse the main text’s oracle ranking after changing the stopping behavior, but do not explain that change precisely enough to reproduce it. The fixed-iteration experiments mitigate this concern for the central calibrated contribution.
